what_its_for: Chlorhexidine is used to kill germs and bacteria. It comes in different forms: a mouth rinse to treat gum disease and mouth sores, and a skin wash to clean skin before surgery or to treat skin infections. It helps reduce harmful bacteria in your mouth or on your skin.
how_to_take: For mouth rinse: Measure out the amount your dentist or doctor told you to use (usually about half a cap or 15 mL). Swish it around your mouth for 30 seconds, then spit it out completely. Do NOT swallow it. Use it after brushing your teeth. For skin wash: Apply to wet skin, gently rub for several minutes, then rinse off thoroughly. Do not use it near your eyes, ears, or mouth, as it can cause serious irritation. Do not use it on open wounds unless your doctor tells you to.
dosing: Mouth rinse: Usually used twice a day, in the morning and at night, after brushing your teeth. Your dentist may prescribe it for a specific number of weeks. Skin wash: Used as directed by your doctor, usually once before a surgery or procedure, or as needed for skin cleaning. Always follow the exact directions given by your dentist or doctor.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose of the mouth rinse, use it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue your normal schedule. Do not use extra rinse to make up for the missed dose. For the skin wash, follow your healthcare provider's specific instructions.
storage: Store at room temperature, away from heat and direct sunlight. Keep the bottle tightly closed when not in use. Keep it out of reach of children and pets. Do not freeze the mouth rinse. Check the expiration date and do not use it after that date.
what_to_avoid: Do not swallow chlorhexidine mouth rinse, as it can be harmful if swallowed. Avoid getting it in your eyes, ears, or inner ear, as it can cause permanent hearing loss or eye damage. Do not use it on open cuts or wounds unless directed by your doctor. Avoid eating, drinking, or rinsing your mouth with water right after using the mouth rinse, as this reduces how well it works. The mouth rinse may stain your teeth, tongue, or dental work over time, so regular dental cleanings are important.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or dentist right away if you notice: a severe allergic reaction such as rash, hives, swelling of your face or throat, or trouble breathing; severe mouth irritation, pain, or sores that get worse; any signs of a skin reaction like redness, burning, or blistering after using the skin wash; changes in your taste that do not go away; or any side effects that worry you.
when_it_works: For gum disease and mouth infections, you may start to notice improvement within a few days to a week of regular use. For best results, use it exactly as directed for the full recommended period. For skin cleaning before surgery, it works immediately to reduce bacteria on your skin.
special_populations: Children: The mouth rinse is generally not recommended for children under 18 unless specifically directed by a dentist or doctor. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Talk to your doctor before using chlorhexidine if you are pregnant or breastfeeding, as safety has not been fully established. Older adults: Use with the same caution as other adults, but be especially careful not to swallow the rinse. Allergies: Tell your doctor if you have ever had a reaction to chlorhexidine or similar products before using it.
